children: JD.com (JD) shares fell 6.03% to $25.88 at 9:50 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 17, after the Chinese e-commerce group reported third-quarter results that showed a sharp profit rebound but only modest sales growth. Management also struck a cautious tone on electronics demand for the fourth quarter and 2027.

Net revenues rose 3.5% to RMB309.6 billion ($46.2 billion), and non-GAAP net income attributable to shareholders climbed to RMB8.3 billion from RMB5.8 billion. GAAP operating income swung to RMB5.2 billion from a loss of RMB1.1 billion as new-business losses, led by food delivery, narrowed to RMB9.6 billion from RMB15.7 billion. JD Retail's operating margin slipped to 5.8% from 5.9%. On the call, management cited price increases and subsidy timing as headwinds for electronics, Investing.com reported in its call coverage.

The core retail engine is not widening margins, so the profit jump came mostly from spending less on food delivery. That lever still has room, since management targets a significant cut in food delivery investment in 2027, but it is a cost story rather than a growth story. GuruFocus gives JD a GF Score of 78/100, with balanced profitability and financial strength. Its GF Value of $39.87 implies a 35% discount, which GuruFocus rates significantly undervalued, though a stalled retail margin is the kind of detail that keeps value gaps open. The next test is fourth-quarter electronics sales and the pace of food delivery cuts.

title: JD.com Stocks Fall 6.03% as Cautious Electronics Outlook Overshadows Profit Jump
